note: THE S9d REAL-PATH WALK, executable (cinatra#2788, PR #2939).
ROUND 4 RE-WALKED C2 AND C6 ONLY, on a run of their own, after the settled branch of the
card was fixed (no supersede line on a settled card; no floor at all on a FIRED one-off).
So the proof set now spans THREE runs, and README.md says which cell belongs to which.
Everything below is the walk as it stands and is driven step by step; a pass that re-shoots
part of the set drives the steps it needs and declares cells only for the cells it re-shoots.
ROUND 3 REDRAWS THE PROOF SET, because round 2 photographed a composition the plan does not
contain: the configuration opened INSIDE the rail column, under its own row, with the agentic
run progress card beside it. Plan (A) §7.2 step 5 / §7.4 step 7 as amended: 'open that step to
see the configuration or change it — it opens to the right of the steps, never directly under a
step, and no agentic run progress card is shown with it.' So the cells now walk the schedule
through its THREE STAGES on BOTH page hosts, which is what a reader has to be able to see:
first shown       -> C1 (chat: the stated schedule, Confirm)      · C7 (run page: the run's
standard scheduling step, the same form with Continue)
configured, not   -> C2 (chat: after Confirm, the rows and Save   · C3 (run page: the schedule
run                  changes)                                      step selected — rail left,
form right, no progress card)
ran               -> C6 (chat: the card after the one-off fired)  · C8 (run page: the run's
steps, the schedule step
still in the rail)
C5 (the expired reading) rides along as an extra cell, on its own untouched proposal.
TWO OF THE SIX CELLS CANNOT BE RECORDS OF THIS INDEX, and the steps that reach them say so
rather than declaring a cell that would be refused at the shutter. This index is the LIFECYCLE-CARD
index: every record it holds asserts `[data-lifecycle-card-host="<host>"]` on the screen it
photographs (`requiredAssertionsFor` in `scripts/ci/lib/capture-record-contract.mjs`, which asks
for it with or without a kind). C7 is the run's SETUP scheduling step — the shipped trigger
screen, which draws no lifecycle card — and C8 is the run detail AFTER the fire, where the
schedule is a rail ROW and its surface is not drawn. Both screens are real and both are owed as
pictures; neither can be an honest record here without inventing an anchor for the recorder to
count, so the walk drives to them, names them, and leaves the pictures to the capture lane.
README.md carries that as the open deviation.
IT SAYS WHERE TO STAND AND WHAT TO PRESS. It never says what was seen: every assertion in every
record it produces is counted off the live page by `observeCapture`, and a cell that does not
come out fails AT THE CELL rather than at the end of a round nobody can repeat.
NOTHING HERE IS SEEDED. The schedule is STATED by typing a sentence into the shipped composer;
the scripted model bridge answers it by calling the shipped producer `schedule_proposal_render`
over self-MCP; the proposal ref is the product's own. That is why the sentence is an action and
the thread has no address in this file — the product mints it, and the dark context FOLLOWS the
light one to wherever it landed.
ONE ONE-OFF, AND THE WALK NEVER FIRES IT. The 'ran' stage is the card after a one-off has fired
(§7.2: 'once a one-off has fired it cannot be changed'), and the whole worth of that stage is
that the schedule came DUE — so no step here presses 'Run now', and no step releases the trigger.
Confirm mints the run; the run page's schedule step is C3; the shipped delayed job releases the
one-off at the time the person stated; and the SAME conversation, reopened afterwards, is C6.
`after-fire` CANNOT WAIT ON THE FLOOR OR ON A RELEASED LINE, because a fired one-off draws
neither: plan (A) §7.2 — "once a one-off has fired it cannot be changed" — so the card withdraws
Save changes, Cancel schedule and Run now together with the status line that used to explain them.
A settled card exists the moment Confirm is pressed, so waiting on that alone would let a run
photograph C6 before the schedule was ever due. TWO THINGS therefore gate the cell, and they are
named rather than implied: the LANE polls `agent_run_triggers.released_at` in the database and
drives this step only once the release job has stamped it — the fire is a database fact, not a
selector — and the step then waits for the READ-ONLY rows the fired card draws
(`[data-field="schedule-run-at"][disabled]`), which is the painted half of the same reading.
AND THE SELECTOR ALONE DOES NOT ESTABLISH FIRING — said here so nobody reads it as the
proof. `canSaveInstalled` refuses a save for THREE different reasons — released, arming,
or a one-off whose instant is no longer in the future — so the read-only rows also stand
on an arming card and on a past-due card whose gate has not opened yet. Only
`released_at` separates those, and this file cannot poll a database: the lane does, and a
cell driven without that gate would be honestly framed and wrongly timed.
C7 was round 3's only cell on another run, and it has to be: an armed run's setup scheduling
step is behind it, and only a fresh run still shows it. Round 3's proof set was therefore ONE
run for every stage the schedule passes through, plus that fresh run; round 4 then added its own.
TWO PASSES, because the clock is real. `PROPOSAL_TTL_SECONDS = 1800`: the expired reading is
reached by letting the shipped window actually run out, not by moving a clock. Pass 1 starts
that window and walks the one-off; pass 2 runs after it has elapsed and walks C5.
export WALK_BASE=... WALK_COOKIE=... WALK_TEMPLATE_ID=... WALK_TEMPLATE_SLUG=...
node scripts/audit/lib/chat-hitl-capture-driver.mjs --walk evidence/2788-s9d-rework/capture-walk.json \
--steps expired-clock,state-the-schedule,follow-dark,confirm,confirm-dark
# ...with WALK_RUN_ID and WALK_SETUP_RUN_ID read from the lane:
node scripts/audit/lib/chat-hitl-capture-driver.mjs --walk evidence/2788-s9d-rework/capture-walk.json \
--steps setup-scheduling-step,run-page,run-page-dark
# ...after the one-off has come due on its own, and after the window elapses,
# with WALK_THREAD and WALK_EXPIRED_THREAD read from the operator's environment:
node scripts/audit/lib/chat-hitl-capture-driver.mjs --walk evidence/2788-s9d-rework/capture-walk.json \
--steps after-fire,after-fire-dark
node scripts/audit/lib/chat-hitl-capture-driver.mjs --walk evidence/2788-s9d-rework/capture-walk.json \
--steps expired,expired-dark
# C7 and C8 are taken outside the recorder — see drivers/page-control.mjs.
THE LANE SUPPLIES THE IDS, NOT THIS FILE. `${WALK_BASE}`, `${WALK_COOKIE}`, `${WALK_TEMPLATE_ID}`,
`${WALK_TEMPLATE_SLUG}`, `${WALK_RUN_ID}`, `${WALK_SETUP_RUN_ID}`, `${WALK_THREAD}` and
`${WALK_EXPIRED_THREAD}` are
the operator's environment. A committed plan carrying a host, a port, a session or one lane's row
ids is a leak and a plan the next lane cannot run. The run ids are read out of the lane's own
`agent_runs`, which is the same source every row of TIMELINE.md is read from.
EVERY CELL IS `window`-FRAMED. That is the maintainer's first rejection of round 1 turned into a
declaration the record carries: the browser window as the operator sees it — the navigation, both
conversation turns and the composer around the card, or the whole run surface with both columns
in view — not the scrolled-out document.
C4 IS ABSENT AND STAYS ABSENT. It asked for the review page carrying THIS run's real artifact
review, and this run has none: a schedule decides WHEN the agent runs, and a review card exists
only after it has run and produced something a lane with a model-provider credential can make. A
lane that may hold one owns that cell. A stand-in is never acceptable, so there is no C4 step here
to accidentally answer with the wrong screen.

steps.why: Start the shipped 30-minute window on a proposal nobody will touch. No cell: this step only makes the clock real.

actions.text: Please schedule ${WALK_TEMPLATE_ID} — I want it to run once, a few minutes from now.

steps.why: STAGE 1 in the conversation: the ONE-OFF as the person states it, photographed BEFORE Confirm. The assistant answers the sentence with the card; the person then states the schedule ON THE CARD — the option rows are editable until Confirm, which is the plan's own sentence — choosing Schedule for later and putting the run-at and the timezone in. There is no going back once Confirm is pressed, so C1 is shot in both themes first.

actions.text: Please schedule ${WALK_TEMPLATE_ID} — I want it to run once, a few minutes from now.

cells.requires: FIRST SHOWN in the conversation: the ONE-OFF the person stated, the three option rows editable with Schedule for later chosen and owning Run at / Timezone, and Confirm alone on the floor

steps.why: The SAME thread and the SAME proposal in dark. It is followed rather than navigated to: the product minted the thread, so this file does not know its address. The person's statement is a CLIENT reading until Confirm — the proposal on the server still carries what the assistant proposed — so this context states the same one-off on the same card rather than pretending a reload would carry it.

THE PRESS, and STAGE 2 in the conversation: one press, on the shipped control, on the card the PREVIOUS STEP drove — the same context, the same page, no navigation in between — which is what makes C2 the same card in the same place rather than another card that looks settled. That identity is carried by the walk's own actions and by C2's record (one card instance on one thread URL, Confirm gone from the card root); it is not read off a before/after picture pair unless the same pass also shoots C1.

cells.requires: CONFIGURED, NOT RUN: the SAME card in the SAME place after Confirm — the same rows, Save changes, no status label, no summary box

steps.why: The configured reading in dark, on the thread this context is already on.

cells.requires: the same configured reading in dark

steps.why: STAGE 1 on the run page (C7): the run's own scheduling step — 'When should this run?' over the three option rows and Continue — on a FRESH run that has not been armed. NO CELL: this screen draws no lifecycle card, so it cannot carry a record of this index; the picture is owed to the capture lane (see README).

STAGE 2 on the run page (C3): the schedule step of the run the walk armed at `confirm`, reached by a REAL press of the rail row — the rail on the left, the form in the run detail on the right, and no run progress beside it, because this run has not run.

cells.requires: CONFIGURED, NOT RUN on the run page: the step rail on the LEFT with Schedule selected, the form in the run detail on the RIGHT with Save changes / Cancel schedule / Run now, nothing under the rail row, and NO agentic run progress card anywhere in the window

steps.why: The same step in dark, on the same run.

STAGE 3 in the conversation (C6): the SAME card in the SAME thread once the one-off has FIRED ON ITS OWN at the time the person stated — the schedule cannot be changed any more, and the card withdraws every control rather than drawing one that only refuses. Nothing in this walk releases it: the shipped delayed job does, the lane waits for `released_at` in the database before this step is driven, and the step waits for the read-only rows the fired card draws. The card itself is scrolled into the middle of the window, because a fired card has no floor to centre on.

cells.requires: RAN: the same card in the same conversation after the one-off fired — the same rows, and Save changes no longer offered

steps.why: The same reading in dark, on the thread the light context is on.

cells.requires: the same ran reading in dark

steps.why: The expired reading, after the shipped window has actually run out. The proposal is the one `expired-clock` minted and nothing touched.

cells.requires: the expired reading: still visible, still editable, Confirm offered and nothing else on the floor

steps.why: The expired reading in dark, on the thread the light context is on.
